chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muhammad ibn Aslam, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the man who buys all the goods for a price, then he evaluates each garment at what it is worth, until the total capital of his wealth is covered. Can he sell it for a profit? He said: No, until he clarifies to him that he has fixed the price.

key_terms.الْمُرَابَحَة: Reselling at a fixed profit margin

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for legally reselling bulk goods for a profit in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) clarifies that merely valuing individual items to cover the total capital is insufficient for permissible resale (murabahah); the buyer must explicitly fix the selling price for each item to avoid ambiguity (gharar). This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on precise price determination in trade contracts to ensure fairness and prevent hidden defects in the transaction.
